ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure labels four resonance forms from left to right: (I) is H2C=N+=N−, with the central nitrogen positively charged and the terminal nitrogen negatively charged; (II) is H2C+−N=N−, with carbon positively charged and the terminal nitrogen negatively charged; (III) is H2C−−N+≡N, with carbon negatively charged, and the nitrogen connected to it positively charged and forming a triple bond with the terminal nitrogen; (IV) is H2C−−N=N+, with carbon negatively charged and the terminal nitrogen positively charged. Reasoning: When comparing the stability of resonance structures, first consider closed-shell structures satisfying the octet, then consider whether the charge distribution conforms to electronegativity. In I and III, all atoms can satisfy the octet, so they are more stable than II and IV. Comparing I and III, the negative charge in I is on the more electronegative nitrogen, while the negative charge in III is on the less electronegative carbon, so I is more stable. Comparing II and IV, in II the negative charge is on nitrogen and the positive charge is on carbon; IV puts the negative charge on carbon and has the terminal nitrogen positively charged and electron-deficient, which is more unfavorable, so II is more stable than IV. Therefore the stability order is I > III > II > IV.

method.method_draft: First describe the image structures and label the charge/bond pattern for I–IV. Check octets: I and III are closed-octet contributors, while II has an electron-deficient carbocation carbon and IV has an unfavorable electron-deficient/positively charged terminal nitrogen arrangement. Rank the closed-octet forms first. Between I and III, prefer I because its negative charge is on nitrogen, whereas III has negative charge on carbon. Between II and IV, prefer II because the negative charge is on nitrogen and the positive charge is on carbon, while IV reverses this favorable electronegativity pattern and puts positive charge on terminal N. Therefore obtain I > III > II > IV.

图像描述：图中从左到右标出四个共振式：(I) 为 H2C=N+=N−，中央氮带正电、末端氮带负电；(II) 为 H2C+−N=N−，碳带正电、末端氮带负电；(III) 为 H2C−−N+≡N，碳带负电、与其相连的氮带正电并与末端氮形成三键；(IV) 为 H2C−−N=N+，碳带负电、末端氮带正电。
推理：比较共振结构稳定性时，优先考虑满足八隅体的闭壳层结构，再考虑电荷分布是否符合电负性。I 和 III 中各原子均可满足八隅体，因此比 II 和 IV 稳定。I 与 III 比较，I 的负电荷在更电负性的氮上，而 III 的负电荷在较不电负性的碳上，所以 I 更稳定。II 与 IV 比较，II 中负电荷在氮上、正电荷在碳上；IV 则把负电荷放在碳上且末端氮带正电并电子不足，更不利，所以 II 比 IV 稳定。故稳定性顺序为 I > III > II > IV。

method.method_draft: After reading the image, recognize the molecule as CH2N2 resonance. Treat I as the canonical diazo contributor, which is most stable because it keeps the diazo C=N^+=N^- pattern and places negative charge on terminal nitrogen. Treat III as the secondary diazonium-ylide contributor: the N≡N bond is stabilizing, but the carbon bears negative charge, so it is below I. Treat II as a minor carbocationic contributor because the carbon is electron-deficient despite having negative charge on terminal nitrogen. Treat IV as the least stable contributor because it lacks the stabilizing N≡N bond and places positive charge on terminal nitrogen while carbon is negative. This gives I > III > II > IV.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中给出了 CH2N2 的四个共振式，依次标为 (I)、(II)、(III)、(IV)。(I) 显示为 H2C=N+=N− 型，中心氮带正电、末端氮带负电；(II) 显示为 H2C+−N=N− 型，碳带正电、末端氮带负电；(III) 显示为 H2C−−N+≡N 型，碳带负电，并含有 N≡N 三键；(IV) 显示为 H2C−−N=N+ 型，碳带负电、末端氮带正电，且没有 N≡N 三键。

推理：这是重氮甲烷 CH2N2 的共振结构稳定性比较。(I) 是典型的重氮主要贡献式，具有 C=N+=N− 的稳定重氮形式，并且负电荷位于电负性较大的末端氮上，所以最稳定。(III) 含有较强的 N≡N 三键，且整体八隅体较好，因此比 (II) 和 (IV) 稳定；但它把负电荷放在碳上，所以稳定性低于 (I)。(II) 是碳正离子型贡献式，碳电子不足，稳定性较差，但负电荷仍在末端氮上，因此比 (IV) 稍稳定。(IV) 同时把负电荷放在碳上、正电荷放在末端氮上，并且缺少 N≡N 三键的稳定化作用，所以最不稳定。因此稳定性顺序为 (I) > (III) > (II) > (IV)。
